title: Definitions
novel:
Ted stood before his first class, fingers shaking around the [[syllabus|syllabus]]. He was a [[professor|professor]] now, and the title felt too large for him. He opened his mouth and [[stuttered|stutter]]. A student laughed, and Ted's face grew hot.

Meanwhile, Barney and Robin sat in the booth, refusing to [[define|define]] what they were. "[[Labels|label]] are for cans," Barney said. Robin nodded, [[reluctant|reluctant]] to admit anything deeper.

"You two are clearly more than friends," Lily said.

Barney [[hesitated|hesitate]]. Robin looked away. It was, Ted later said, the most [[awkward|awkward]] silence of the year.

That evening Ted returned to the bar, exhausted but [[confident|confident]] for the first time. His [[lecture|lecture]] had not been perfect, but he had survived it.

"So what are you two, really?" Ted asked.

They exchanged a glance. "We're two friends who help each other," Barney said, as if reading from a [[mutual|mutual]] script they had [[pretended|pretend]] to believe.

Robin smiled, a small [[relief|relief]] crossing her face. Some definitions, Ted [[realized|realize]], were best left unwritten.

syllabus.en: a list of the subjects to be taught in a course

professor.en: a teacher of the highest rank in a university

stutter.en: to speak with difficulty, repeating sounds

define.en: to say exactly what something means

label.en: a word that describes someone or something

hesitate.en: to pause before doing something because you are unsure

awkward.en: making people feel shy or uncomfortable

confident.en: sure that you can do something well

lecture.en: a talk given to teach a group of students

mutual.en: shared by two or more people

pretend.en: to act as if something is true when it is not

relief.en: the good feeling when something unpleasant stops
